The National Debt has topped £3 trillion for the first time in the official figures.
The headline rate of inflation has hit 3.5% and is surely heading back up to 4% in the coming months.

articles.title: Inflation and government borrowing highest for a year ahead of next week's Budget
articles.description: Inflation accelerated to 3.5% from 3.1% in the year to September, according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS).
articles.summary: UK inflation and government borrowing both hit their highest in a year on Wednesday, adding to the pressure on Chancellor John Healey ahead of his first Budget in a week.
key_points: The pace of UK price rises accelerated to 3.5% in the year to September, pushed up by sharp increases in petrol and diesel prices.
The inflation figures came as UK government borrowing jumped to nearly £25bn in September, which means borrowing for the financial year to date is running £6bn above official forecasts.
Healey has promised a Budget which will keep to Labour's commitment not to hike the three main taxes - income tax, National Insurance and VAT - while sticking to the party's fiscal rules.

articles.title: AI-Enabled FP&A Orchestration: Evolution, Gaps & Pathways
articles.summary: When you watch a symphony orchestra, you can see the conductor, the musicians and the instruments, but what is really magical is the invisible architecture that keeps them together: coordination.
key_points: The conductor is FP&A itself: setting direction, owning the decision, and remaining accountable for the outcome.
The musicians are our analysts and finance teams: providing the judgement and business context that no system can ever replace.
The instruments are our AI agents and data systems: continuous, scalable, and built to run in parallel.

articles.title: Measuring the Invisible: How CFOs Must Evaluate FP&A Talent in an AI-First Function — Part 3 of 3
articles.summary: Why output metrics fail in agentic finance — and what to measure instead.
key_points: In Parts 1 and 2, I argued that agentic AI does not shrink the FP&A role so much as relocate it [1] [2].
The routine production of a variance pack or a driver-based forecast moves to the agent; what remains for the professional is judgment in the probabilistic zone that the agent cannot be trusted to…
Part 1 set out the capability that judgment requires — the FP&A Agent Manager and a four-layer stack: Data & Tooling Literacy, Probabilistic Model Behaviour, Probability Theory, Control Design.
